title: M2Det: A Single-Shot Object Detector based on Multi-Level Feature Pyramid Network
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence

problem.summary: Scale variation is a major detection challenge, and while feature pyramids help, existing detectors (SSD, FPN, STDN) build them by simply reusing the backbone layers designed for classification. As a result each pyramid level is not sufficiently representative for detection, and every feature map carries mostly single-level information rather than a mix of shallow localization cues and deep semantics.
statements: Scale variation across object instances is one of the major challenges for the object detection task.
Detecting over an image pyramid greatly increases memory and computational complexity, dropping efficiency dramatically.
Feature maps taken from classification-oriented backbone layers are not representative enough for the object detection task.
Each pyramid level is built mainly from single-level backbone features, although high-level features favor classification while low-level features favor localization and simple appearances.

evidence.quote: Scale variation across object instances is one of the major challenges for the object detection task
this solution will greatly increase memory and computational complexity, thus the efficiency of such object detectors drop dramatically.
they simply construct the feature pyramid according to the inherent multi-scale, pyramidal architecture of the backbones which are actually designed for object classification task.

each feature map in the pyramid (used for detecting objects in a specific range of size) is mainly or even solely constructed from single-level layers of the backbone, that is, it mainly or only contains single-level information.

background.summary: The paper situates itself between the two standard responses to scale variation: featurized image pyramids (accurate but costly, e.g. SNIP) and feature pyramids built from network layers (SSD, MS-CNN, FPN, DSSD, YOLOv3, RetinaNet, RefineDet). It also builds on squeeze-and-excitation channel attention for the aggregation stage.

relatedWork.name: SSD
relatedWork.relation: base detector whose pyramid style M2Det replaces and whose architecture it adopts
relatedWork.quote: SSD (Liu et al. 2016) directly and independently uses two layers of the backbone (i.e. VGG16) and four extra layers obtained by stride 2 convolution to construct the feature pyramid

relatedWork.name: FPN
relatedWork.quote: FPN (Lin et al. 2017a) constructs the feature pyramid by fusing the deep and shallow layers in a top-down manner.

relatedWork.name: STDN
relatedWork.relation: prior pyramid built from a DenseNet dense block
relatedWork.quote: STDN (Zhou et al. 2018) only uses the last dense block of DenseNet (Huang et al. 2017) to construct feature pyramid by pooling and scale-transfer operations

relatedWork.name: SNIP
relatedWork.relation: image-pyramid strategy that is accurate but too costly for real time
relatedWork.quote: Despite the performance gain, such a strategy could be costly time-wise and memory-wise, which forbid its application in real-time tasks.

relatedWork.name: RefineDet
relatedWork.quote: RefineDet (Zhang et al. 2018) adopted two-step cascade regression, which achieves a remarkable progress on accuracy while keeping the efficiency of SSD.

relatedWork.name: Squeeze-and-Excitation networks
relatedWork.relation: source of the channel attention used in SFAM
relatedWork.quote: Following SE block (Hu, Shen, and Sun 2017), we use global average pooling to generate channel-wise statistics

evidence.quote: The second one is detecting objects in the feature pyramid extracted from inherent layers within the network while merely taking a single-scale image.

In general, high-level features in the deeper layers are more discriminative for classification subtask while low-level features in the shallower layers can be helpful for object location regression sub-task.

solution.summary: MLFPN constructs the pyramid from decoder features of stacked Thinned U-shape Modules instead of raw backbone layers: FFMv1 fuses shallow and deep backbone features into a base feature, alternating TUMs and FFMv2s extract multi-level multi-scale features, and SFAM concatenates same-scale features across levels and reweights them with squeeze-and-excitation channel attention. Integrating MLFPN into SSD yields the one-stage detector M2Det.
solution.approach: Fuse multi-level backbone features into a base feature, refine them through alternating thinned U-shape and feature-fusion modules, then aggregate same-scale outputs across levels with channel attention to form the detection pyramid.
components: Feature Fusion Module v1 (FFMv1) producing the base feature from conv4_3 and conv5_3
Thinned U-shape Modules (TUM) with strided 3x3 encoder and upsample+sum decoder
Feature Fusion Module v2 (FFMv2) feeding base feature into each subsequent TUM
Scale-wise Feature Aggregation Module (SFAM): channel-wise concatenation plus SE attention
8 TUMs with 6 output scales and 256 channels per scale by default
SSD-style dense prediction heads with two conv layers per pyramid level
soft-NMS with linear kernel for post-processing

evidence.quote: we present Multi-Level Feature Pyramid Network (MLFPN) to construct more effective feature pyramids for detecting objects of different scales.
First, we fuse multi-level features (i.e. multiple layers) extracted by backbone as the base feature.
we gather up the decoder layers with equivalent scales (sizes) to construct a feature pyramid for object detection, in which every feature map consists of the layers (features) from multiple levels.
SFAM aggregates the features into the multi-level feature pyramid through a scale-wise feature concatenation operation and an adaptive attention mechanism.

experiments.summary: Evaluation is on MS-COCO (trainval35k for training, test-dev for the main comparison, minival for ablations): an ablation adds TUMs, base feature and SFAM step by step over an SSD baseline, a variant study sweeps TUM count and channel width, and a speed-accuracy comparison covers one- and two-stage detectors at 320/512/800 inputs with single- and multi-scale inference.

benchmarks.split: minival, full M2Det with SFAM, VGG-16 320x320
test-dev, M2Det single-scale inference on Titan X

evidence.quote: M2Det achieves AP of 41.0 at speed of 11.8 FPS with single-scale inference strategy and AP of 44.2 with multi-scale inference strategy
M2Det-320 with VGG backbone achieves AP of 38.9, which has surpassed most object detectors with more powerful backbones and larger input size
draws a significantly better speed-accuracy curve compared with other methods.

limitations.summary: Training is very expensive (up to 14 days for the best model), the headline 41.0/44.2 numbers rely on 800x800 inputs and multi-scale testing, batch size is memory-constrained on 12GB GPUs, and the ImageNet-pretrained backbones plus soft-NMS post-processing keep it in the standard slow pipeline.
items: Training cost is high: 3 and 6 days for the VGG-16 320/512 models on 4 Titan X devices, 11 days for ResNet-101 512 on 2 V100s, and 14 days for the best 800x800 model.
The headline 41.0 AP single-scale result requires the 800x800 input variant; smaller 320 input reaches only 38.9 AP.
Memory limits batch size (only 4 available for ResNet-101 512), which also slows training.
Backbones must be pre-trained on ImageNet before M2Det training.

evidence.quote: The most accurate model is M2Det with the VGG backbone and 800×800 input size, it costs 14 days.
M2Det with the input size of 512 is not only limited in the batch size (only 4 is available), but also takes a long time to train
the backbones need to be pre-trained on the ImageNet 2012 dataset

equations.name: Multi-level multi-scale features
equations.expr: x_i^l = T_l(X_base) for l=1; x_i^l = T_l(F(X_base, x_i^{l-1})) for l=2..L

equations.name: SE excitation
equations.expr: s = F_ex(z, W) = sigma(W2 * delta(W1 * z))

deploymentClaims: 11.8 FPS single-scale inference with 41.0 AP on MS COCO test-dev, measured with batch size 1 on a single NVIDIA Titan X PASCAL
ResNet-101 variant runs at 15.8 FPS with 38.8 AP based on PyTorch optimizations
PyTorch implementation; code released at github.com/qijiezhao/M2Det

evidence.quote: which are produced by testing it on MS-COCO test-dev split, with a single NVIDIA Titan X PASCAL and the batch size 1.
